content.thinking: The user wants a bash script that monitors queue depth and sends alerts when thresholds are exceeded. Let me create a comprehensive monitoring script. I'll look at existing monitoring scripts for patterns.

content.text: I'll create a queue depth monitoring script with configurable thresholds, multiple alert channels, and a clean structure.

content.content:
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	#
3	# System Resource Monitor
4	# Monitors CPU, memory, and disk usage; sends alerts when thresholds are exceeded.
5	
6	set -euo pipefail
7	
8	# --- Configuration (override via environment) ---
9	CPU_THRESHOLD="${CPU_THRESHOLD:-80}"
10	MEM_THRESHOLD="${MEM_THRESHOLD:-80}"
11	DISK_THRESHOLD="${DISK_THRESHOLD:-90}"
12	CHECK_INTERVAL="${CHECK_INTERVAL:-60}"   # seconds between checks
13	LOG_FILE="${LOG_FILE:-/var/log/system_monitor.log}"
14	ALERT_METHOD="${ALERT_METHOD:-log}"      # log | email | slack
15	SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL="${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL:-}"
16	ALERT_EMAIL="${ALERT_EMAIL:-}"
17	
18	# Cooldown: avoid spamming the same alert every cycle
19	declare -A LAST_ALERTED
20	COOLDOWN=300  # seconds before the same alert can fire again
21	
22	log() {
23	    local msg="[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $1"
24	    echo "$msg"
25	    echo "$msg" >> "$LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
26	}
27	
28	send_alert() {
29	    local subject="$1"
30	    local body="$2"
31	    local key="$3"
32	
33	    # Cooldown check
34	    local now
35	    now=$(date +%s)
36	    if [[ -n "${LAST_ALERTED[$key]:-}" ]]; then
37	        local elapsed=$(( now - LAST_ALERTED[$key] ))
38	        if (( elapsed < COOLDOWN )); then
39	            return 0
40	        fi
41	    fi
42	    LAST_ALERTED[$key]=$now
43	
44	    log "ALERT: $subject — $body"
45	
46	    case "$ALERT_METHOD" in
47	        email)
48	            if [[ -n "$ALERT_EMAIL" ]] && command -v mail &>/dev/null; then
49	                echo "$body" | mail -s "$subject" "$ALERT_EMAIL"
50	            fi
51	            ;;
52	        slack)
53	            if [[ -n "$SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL" ]] && command -v curl &>/dev/null; then
54	                curl -sf -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' \
55	                    --data "{\"text\":\":warning: *$subject*\n$body\"}" \
56	                    "$SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
57	            fi
58	            ;;
59	        log) ;;  # already logged above
60	    esac
61	}
62	
63	check_cpu() {

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	set -euo pipefail
3	
4	# Configuration
5	THRESHOLD=${DISK_THRESHOLD:-80}
6	TARGET_DIRS=(${CLEANUP_DIRS:-"/tmp /var/log"})
7	MAX_AGE_DAYS=${MAX_AGE:-30}
8	LOG_FILE=${LOG_FILE:-"/var/log/disk_monitor.log"}
9	DRY_RUN=${DRY_RUN:-false}
10	
11	log() {
12	    local level="$1"
13	    shift
14	    local msg="[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] [$level] $*"
15	    echo "$msg" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "$msg"
16	}
17	
18	check_disk_usage() {
19	    local mount="${1:-/}"
20	    local usage
21	    usage=$(df "$mount" | awk 'NR==2 {gsub(/%/,""); print $5}')
22	    echo "$usage"
23	}
24	
25	find_old_files() {
26	    local dir="$1"
27	    local age="$2"
28	    if [[ ! -d "$dir" ]]; then
29	        log "WARN" "Directory does not exist: $dir"
30	        return 1
31	    fi
32	    find "$dir" -type f -mtime +"$age" -print 2>/dev/null
33	}
34	
35	cleanup_file() {
36	    local file="$1"
37	    if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
38	        log "DRY-RUN" "Would delete: $file"
39	        return 0
40	    fi
41	    if rm -f "$file" 2>>"$LOG_FILE"; then
42	        log "INFO" "Deleted: $file"
43	        return 0
44	    else
45	        log "ERROR" "Failed to delete: $file"
46	        return 1
47	    fi
48	}
49	
50	main() {
51	    log "INFO" "Starting disk monitor (threshold=${THRESHOLD}%, max_age=${MAX_AGE_DAYS}d, dry_run=${DRY_RUN})"
52	
53	    local usage
54	    usage=$(check_disk_usage "/")
55	    log "INFO" "Current disk usage: ${usage}%"
56	
57	    if (( usage < THRESHOLD )); then
58	        log "INFO" "Disk usage ${usage}% is below threshold ${THRESHOLD}%. No action needed."
59	        exit 0
60	    fi
61	
62	    log "WARN" "Disk usage ${usage}% exceeds threshold ${THRESHOLD}%. Starting cleanup..."
63	
64	    local deleted=0
65	    local failed=0
66	
67	    for dir in "${TARGET_DIRS[@]}"; do
68	        log "INFO" "Scanning: $dir"
69	        while IFS= read -r file; do
70	            [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue
71	            if cleanup_file "$file"; then
72	                ((deleted++))
73	            else
74	                ((failed++))
75	            fi
76	        done < <(find_old_files "$dir" "$MAX_AGE_DAYS")
77	    done
78	
79	    local new_usage
80	    new_usage=$(check_disk_usage "/")
81	    log "INFO" "Cleanup complete. Files deleted: $deleted, failed: $failed"
82	    log "INFO" "Disk usage after cleanup: ${new_usage}%"
83	
84	    if (( new_usage >= THRESHOLD )); then
85	        log "WARN" "Disk usage still above threshold after cleanup. Manual intervention may be required."
86	        exit 1
87	    fi
88	
89	    log "INFO" "Disk usage restored below threshold."
90	    exit 0
91	}
92	
93	main "$@"
94

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Queue Depth Monitor
# Monitors queue depth and sends alerts when thresholds are exceeded.
# Supports multiple queue backends: RabbitMQ, Redis, AWS SQS, custom script.

set -euo pipefail

# --- Configuration (override via environment) ---
QUEUE_BACKEND="${QUEUE_BACKEND:-custom}"          # rabbitmq | redis | sqs | custom
WARNING_THRESHOLD="${WARNING_THRESHOLD:-1000}"     # warning alert threshold
CRITICAL_THRESHOLD="${CRITICAL_THRESHOLD:-5000}"   # critical alert threshold
CHECK_INTERVAL="${CHECK_INTERVAL:-30}"             # seconds between checks
LOG_FILE="${LOG_FILE:-/var/log/queue_monitor.log}"
ALERT_METHOD="${ALERT_METHOD:-log}"                # log | email | slack | webhook
SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL="${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL:-}"
ALERT_EMAIL="${ALERT_EMAIL:-}"
WEBHOOK_URL="${WEBHOOK_URL:-}"

# RabbitMQ config
RABBITMQ_HOST="${RABBITMQ_HOST:-localhost}"
RABBITMQ_PORT="${RABBITMQ_PORT:-15672}"
RABBITMQ_USER="${RABBITMQ_USER:-guest}"
RABBITMQ_PASS="${RABBITMQ_PASS:-guest}"
RABBITMQ_VHOST="${RABBITMQ_VHOST:-/}"
RABBITMQ_QUEUES="${RABBITMQ_QUEUES:-}"  # comma-separated queue names, empty = all

# Redis config
REDIS_HOST="${REDIS_HOST:-localhost}"
REDIS_PORT="${REDIS_PORT:-6379}"
REDIS_PASSWORD="${REDIS_PASSWORD:-}"
REDIS_QUEUE_KEYS="${REDIS_QUEUE_KEYS:-}"  # comma-separated list keys

# AWS SQS config
SQS_QUEUE_URLS="${SQS_QUEUE_URLS:-}"  # comma-separated queue URLs
AWS_REGION="${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}"

# Custom script config
CUSTOM_SCRIPT="${CUSTOM_SCRIPT:-}"  # must output one "queue_name depth" pair per line

# Cooldown: avoid spamming the same alert every cycle
declare -A LAST_ALERTED
declare -A ALERT_STATE
COOLDOWN=300  # seconds before the same alert can fire again

# --- Helpers ---

log() {
    local msg="[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $1"
    echo "$msg"
    echo "$msg" >> "$LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
}

send_alert() {
    local severity="$1"
    local queue="$2"
    local depth="$3"
    local key="${queue}:${severity}"

    # Cooldown check
    local now
    now=$(date +%s)
    if [[ -n "${LAST_ALERTED[$key]:-}" ]]; then
        local elapsed=$(( now - LAST_ALERTED[$key] ))
        if (( elapsed < COOLDOWN )); then
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    LAST_ALERTED[$key]=$now

    local subject="Queue Alert [${severity}]: ${queue}"
    local body="Queue '${queue}' depth is ${depth}. "
    case "$severity" in
        warning)  body+="Threshold: ${WARNING_THRESHOLD}" ;;
        critical) body+="Threshold: ${CRITICAL_THRESHOLD}" ;;
        recovered) body+="Back to normal. Was previously alerting." ;;
    esac

    log "${severity^^}: $body"

    case "$ALERT_METHOD" in
        email)
            if [[ -n "$ALERT_EMAIL" ]] && command -v mail &>/dev/null; then
                echo "$body" | mail -s "$subject" "$ALERT_EMAIL"
            fi
            ;;
        slack)
            if [[ -n "$SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL" ]] && command -v curl &>/dev/null; then
                local emoji=":warning:"
                [[ "$severity" == "critical" ]] && emoji=":rotating_light:"
                [[ "$severity" == "recovered" ]] && emoji=":white_check_mark:"
                curl -sf -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' \
                    --data "{\"text\":\"${emoji} *${subject}*\n${body}\"}" \
                    "$SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            fi
            ;;
        webhook)
            if [[ -n "$WEBHOOK_URL" ]] && command -v curl &>/dev/null; then
                curl -sf -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' \
                    --data "{\"severity\":\"${severity}\",\"queue\":\"${queue}\",\"depth\":${depth},\"timestamp\":\"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)\"}" \
                    "$WEBHOOK_URL" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            fi
            ;;
        log) ;;  # already logged above
    esac
}

check_thresholds() {
    local queue="$1"
    local depth="$2"

    if (( depth >= CRITICAL_THRESHOLD )); then
        if [[ "${ALERT_STATE[$queue]:-ok}" != "critical" ]]; then
            ALERT_STATE[$queue]="critical"
            send_alert "critical" "$queue" "$depth"
        fi
    elif (( depth >= WARNING_THRESHOLD )); then
        if [[ "${ALERT_STATE[$queue]:-ok}" == "critical" ]]; then
            # Dropped from critical to warning
            ALERT_STATE[$queue]="warning"
            send_alert "warning" "$queue" "$depth"
        elif [[ "${ALERT_STATE[$queue]:-ok}" != "warning" ]]; then
            ALERT_STATE[$queue]="warning"
            send_alert "warning" "$queue" "$depth"
        fi
    else
        if [[ "${ALERT_STATE[$queue]:-ok}" =~ ^(warning|critical)$ ]]; then
            ALERT_STATE[$queue]="ok"
            send_alert "recovered" "$queue" "$depth"
        fi
    fi
}

# --- Backend: RabbitMQ ---

fetch_rabbitmq() {
    if ! command -v curl &>/dev/null; then
        log "ERROR: curl is required for RabbitMQ backend"
        return 1
    fi

    local api_url="http://${RABBITMQ_HOST}:${RABBITMQ_PORT}/api/queues"
    [[ -n "$RABBITMQ_VHOST" ]] && api_url+="/$(python3 -c "import urllib.parse; print(urllib.parse.quote('${RABBITMQ_VHOST}', safe=''))" 2>/dev/null || echo "$RABBITMQ_VHOST")"

    local response
    response=$(curl -sf -u "${RABBITMQ_USER}:${RABBITMQ_PASS}" "$api_url" 2>/dev/null) || {
        log "ERROR: Failed to connect to RabbitMQ API at ${api_url}"
        return 1
    }

    if [[ -z "$RABBITMQ_QUEUES" ]]; then
        # All queues
        echo "$response" | python3 -c "
import sys, json
queues = json.load(sys.stdin)
for q in queues:
    print(q['name'], q.get('messages', 0))
" 2>/dev/null
    else
        # Specific queues
        IFS=',' read -ra qnames <<< "$RABBITMQ_QUEUES"
        for qname in "${qnames[@]}"; do
            qname=$(echo "$qname" | xargs)  # trim whitespace
            local depth
            depth=$(echo "$response" | python3 -c "
import sys, json
queues = json.load(sys.stdin)
target = '${qname}'
for q in queues:
    if q['name'] == target:
        print(q.get('messages', 0))
        break
else:
    print(-1)
" 2>/dev/null) || depth=-1
            if (( depth >= 0 )); then
                echo "$qname $depth"
            fi
        done
    fi
}

# --- Backend: Redis ---

fetch_redis() {
    if ! command -v redis-cli &>/dev/null; then
        log "ERROR: redis-cli is required for Redis backend"
        return 1
    fi

    local auth_flag=""
    [[ -n "$REDIS_PASSWORD" ]] && auth_flag="-a $REDIS_PASSWORD"

    IFS=',' read -ra keys <<< "$REDIS_QUEUE_KEYS"
    for key in "${keys[@]}"; do
        key=$(echo "$key" | xargs)
        local depth
        depth=$(redis-cli -h "$REDIS_HOST" -p "$REDIS_PORT" $auth_flag llen "$key" 2>/dev/null) || depth=-1
        if [[ "$depth" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
            echo "$key $depth"
        fi
    done
}

# --- Backend: AWS SQS ---

fetch_sqs() {
    if ! command -v aws &>/dev/null; then
        log "ERROR: AWS CLI is required for SQS backend"
        return 1
    fi

    IFS=',' read -ra urls <<< "$SQS_QUEUE_URLS"
    for url in "${urls[@]}"; do
        url=$(echo "$url" | xargs)
        local qname
        qname=$(basename "$url")
        local attrs
        attrs=$(aws sqs get-queue-attributes \
            --queue-url "$url" \
            --attribute-names ApproximateNumberOfMessages \
            --region "$AWS_REGION" \
            --output json 2>/dev/null) || {
            log "ERROR: Failed to fetch SQS queue: $url"
            continue
        }
        local depth
        depth=$(echo "$attrs" | python3 -c "
import sys, json
data = json.load(sys.stdin)
print(data['Attributes']['ApproximateNumberOfMessages'])
" 2>/dev/null) || depth=0
        echo "$qname $depth"
    done
}

# --- Backend: Custom ---

fetch_custom() {
    if [[ -z "$CUSTOM_SCRIPT" ]]; then
        log "ERROR: CUSTOM_SCRIPT must be set for custom backend"
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ ! -x "$CUSTOM_SCRIPT" ]]; then
        log "ERROR: CUSTOM_SCRIPT is not executable: $CUSTOM_SCRIPT"
        return 1
    fi
    "$CUSTOM_SCRIPT"
}

# --- Main ---

fetch_queue_depths() {
    case "$QUEUE_BACKEND" in
        rabbitmq) fetch_rabbitmq ;;
        redis)    fetch_redis ;;
        sqs)      fetch_sqs ;;
        custom)   fetch_custom ;;
        *)
            log "ERROR: Unknown backend: $QUEUE_BACKEND"
            return 1
            ;;
    esac
}

usage() {
    cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") [OPTIONS]

Monitors queue depth and sends alerts when thresholds are exceeded.

Options:
  -b NAME   Queue backend: rabbitmq|redis|sqs|custom (default: $QUEUE_BACKEND)
  -w NUM    Warning threshold          (default: $WARNING_THRESHOLD)
  -c NUM    Critical threshold         (default: $CRITICAL_THRESHOLD)
  -i NUM    Check interval in seconds  (default: $CHECK_INTERVAL)
  -a TYPE   Alert method: log|email|slack|webhook (default: $ALERT_METHOD)
  -e ADDR   Alert email address
  -s URL    Slack webhook URL
  -u URL    Generic webhook URL
  -l PATH   Log file path              (default: $LOG_FILE)
  -1        Run once and exit
  -h        Show this help

Environment variables for backends:
  RabbitMQ: RABBITMQ_HOST, RABBITMQ_PORT, RABBITMQ_USER, RABBITMQ_PASS, RABBITMQ_QUEUES
  Redis:    REDIS_HOST, REDIS_PORT, REDIS_PASSWORD, REDIS_QUEUE_KEYS
  SQS:      SQS_QUEUE_URLS, AWS_REGION
  Custom:   CUSTOM_SCRIPT (must output "queue_name depth" per line)

Examples:
  # Monitor RabbitMQ queues, alert via Slack
  QUEUE_BACKEND=rabbitmq ALERT_METHOD=slack SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=https://hooks.slack.com/... ./queue_monitor.sh

  # Monitor Redis lists, run once
  QUEUE_BACKEND=redis REDIS_QUEUE_KEYS="tasks:pending,tasks:failed" ./queue_monitor.sh -1

  # Monitor SQS with custom webhook
  QUEUE_BACKEND=sqs SQS_QUEUE_URLS="https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/123/my-queue" ALERT_METHOD=webhook WEBHOOK_URL=https://example.com/alerts ./queue_monitor.sh
EOF
    exit 0
}

RUN_ONCE=false

while getopts "b:w:c:i:a:e:s:u:l:1h" opt; do
    case $opt in
        b) QUEUE_BACKEND=$OPTARG ;;
        w) WARNING_THRESHOLD=$OPTARG ;;
        c) CRITICAL_THRESHOLD=$OPTARG ;;
        i) CHECK_INTERVAL=$OPTARG ;;
        a) ALERT_METHOD=$OPTARG ;;
        e) ALERT_EMAIL=$OPTARG ;;
        s) SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=$OPTARG ;;
        u) WEBHOOK_URL=$OPTARG ;;
        l) LOG_FILE=$OPTARG ;;
        1) RUN_ONCE=true ;;
        h) usage ;;
        *) usage ;;
    esac
done

log "Queue monitor started — backend=${QUEUE_BACKEND} warn>${WARNING_THRESHOLD} critical>${CRITICAL_THRESHOLD} every ${CHECK_INTERVAL}s (alert via ${ALERT_METHOD})"

run_check() {
    local has_data=false

    while IFS=' ' read -r queue depth; do
        [[ -z "$queue" ]] && continue
        if [[ ! "$depth" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
            log "WARN: Invalid depth for queue '${queue}': ${depth}"
            continue
        fi
        has_data=true
        log "INFO: Queue '${queue}' depth: ${depth}"
        check_thresholds "$queue" "$depth"
    done < <(fetch_queue_depths 2>/dev/null) || true

    if ! $has_data; then
        log "WARN: No queue data received from backend '${QUEUE_BACKEND}'"
    fi
}

if $RUN_ONCE; then
    run_check
    exit 0
fi

trap 'log "Monitor stopped."; exit 0' INT TERM

while true; do
    run_check
    sleep "$CHECK_INTERVAL"
done
